environment.description: Deployed on EKS 1.29 with Cilium CNI in strict mode. Pod runs in namespace 'prod-exec' with a CiliumNetworkPolicy (apiVersion: cilium.io/v2) that applies L7 HTTP-aware filtering: egress from the pod is denied except to the logging collector on port 9200, and ingress to port 8080 is only permitted from entities with label 'app.kubernetes.io/component=mesh-gateway' (the Istio ingress gateway). The Istio AuthorizationPolicy on the workload requires a valid SPIFFE identity (spiffe://cluster.local/ns/prod-exec/sa/api-gateway) for any request to paths matching '/api/internal/*'. Additionally, the pod's ServiceAccount has an annotation triggering the Hashicorp Vault Agent sidecar which intercepts token issuance and enforces a 'num_uses: 1' lease constraint with a TTL of 45s (shorter than the application's 60s). The Vault policy (path 'transit/sign/exec-svc') requires entity alias matching the pod's projected service account token audience. Token rotation is driven by Vault's own lease revocation (revoke-prefix on the transit backend every 45 seconds), meaning even if a token is captured in-flight, the Vault-side lease is already expired before an attacker can replay it through the gateway path. The CiliumNetworkPolicy also drops any packet with TCP payload containing '/bin/' or 'bash' in the HTTP body via its L7 regex rule (matchPattern: '(?i)(\\x2fbin\\x2f|bash|sh\\s+-c)'), providing defense-in-depth against command injection payloads that bypass authentication.
